title: Retrieval quiz: motivation and organisation structure (2.4, 2.5) and one 9-mark question
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 34 (Pupil PDF: motivation and structure retrieval quiz and one 9-mark justify question.)
intro: Answer from memory, then mark with the mark scheme.

questions.q: What did Taylor believe motivates workers?
questions.a: Money: workers should be paid by results (piece rate)

questions.q: Name the five levels of Maslow's hierarchy from the bottom.
questions.a: Physiological, safety, social (love and belonging), esteem, self-actualisation

questions.q: In Herzberg's theory, give one hygiene factor and one motivator.
questions.a: Hygiene: pay, working conditions, job security. Motivator: recognition, responsibility, achievement
For example: commission, bonus, profit sharing, piece rate

questions.q: Give one non-financial method of motivation.
questions.a: For example: job rotation, job enrichment, job enlargement, empowerment, team working

questions.q: What is a span of control?
questions.a: The number of people a manager is directly responsible for

questions.q: What is a chain of command?
questions.a: The line of authority from the top of the organisation to the bottom

questions.q: Does a flat structure have wide or narrow spans of control?
Give one advantage of a centralised structure.
questions.a: Consistent decisions and tight control from head office

questions.q: Give one advantage of delegating decisions to branch managers.
questions.a: Faster, local decisions and more motivated managers

questions.q: A supermarket chain is choosing between paying its warehouse staff a bonus or introducing team working. Justify which it should choose. (9)
questions.a: Either, if justified: a bonus links pay to output (Taylor), quick to introduce, but costs money and may not last; team working meets social needs (Maslow) and is a motivator (Herzberg), cheaper, but takes time and may not suit repetitive picking. Level 3 (7-9): a justified choice that uses the data, with developed chains of reasoning and a comparison showing why it beats the other option. Level 2 (4-6): reasons for the choice in context but little comparison. Level 1 (1-3): generic points.
